summary: Choose k scores so that the difference between the highest and lowest chosen score is as small as possible.
mainInsight: After sorting, an optimal group of k is always k consecutive values: replacing any outside element with one between the min and max never widens the range. So slide a window of size k and take min(nums[i + k - 1] - nums[i]).
invariant: For window start i, nums[i] is its lowest and nums[i + k - 1] its highest score.

approaches.name: Try every subset of size k
Sort, then fixed-size window
approaches.summary: Sort and compare nums[i + k - 1] - nums[i] for each i.
approaches.spaceComplexity: O(1) to O(n) for the sort

commonMistakes: Off-by-one in the window end (nums[i + k] instead of nums[i + k - 1]).
Loop bound len(nums) - k instead of len(nums) - k + 1, missing the last window.

cards.answer: Sort the scores, then slide a window of k consecutive values. Clue: Only the highest and lowest of the k chosen scores matter, so once the scores are sorted the best choice is a run of k neighbouring values.

promptVariants: Why is an optimal choice always k consecutive values in sorted order?
Prove that you only need to check contiguous windows after sorting.
cards.answer: Take any chosen group with lowest value lo and highest hi. All sorted values between lo and hi are in [lo, hi], and there are at least k of them (the chosen ones are among them). Picking k consecutive ones from that stretch keeps the range within hi - lo. So some window of k consecutive sorted values is at least as good.
keyPoints: Range depends only on min and max
Values between them never widen the range
A consecutive window is at least as good
cards.explanation: This exchange-style argument is what lets you discard all non-contiguous choices.

promptVariants: For scores [1, 5, 6, 14, 15] and k = 3, what is the minimum difference?
cards.explanation: Windows after sorting: [1,5,6] -> 5, [5,6,14] -> 9, [6,14,15] -> 9. The minimum is 5.

incorrectOptionExplanations.1: That is the closest pair (k = 2), not three scores.
incorrectOptionExplanations.9: That is the middle or last window, not the best.
incorrectOptionExplanations.14: That is max - min of all scores (k = n).

promptVariants: How many windows does the loop check for n scores?
What is the correct number of window starts?
cards.explanation: Starts go from 0 to n - k inclusive, so the last window ends at index n - 1.

incorrectOptionExplanations.n - k: Misses the last window ending at n - 1.
incorrectOptionExplanations.n - 1: That is the pair count for k = 2 only.
incorrectOptionExplanations.n: Windows starting after n - k would run past the end.

promptVariants: What is the time complexity of the canonical code?
Derive the running time of sort plus window.
cards.explanation: Sorting costs O(n log n); the window scan is O(n) with O(1) per window.

incorrectOptionExplanations.O(n * k): Each window needs only its two ends, not all k values.
